nodes.summary: `P(X₀ ∈ A₀, …, X_n ∈ A_n)` is the integral over `A₀ × ⋯ × A_{n-1}` of the predictive probability `(α H(A_n) + #{i < n | xᵢ ∈ A_n}) / (α + n)`.
nodes.title: The predictive rule of the urn

nodes.summary: The ties of the Blackwell–MacQueen urn follow the Chinese restaurant process (Pitman 2006, §3.1): for an atomless base measure, the partition of the first `n` draws into groups of equal values has the law `α^{|π|} ∏_{B ∈ π} (|B| - 1)! / α^{(n)}`.
nodes.title: The ties of the Blackwell–MacQueen urn follow the Chinese restaurant process

nodes.summary: The Blackwell–MacQueen urn with parameter `α` and base measure `H`: the joint law of the first `n` draws, where draw `n` has law `polyaUrnPredictive α H xs` given the previous draws `xs` (Blackwell–MacQueen 1973).
nodes.title: Blackwell–MacQueen urn

nodes.summary: Forgetting the last draw restricts the tie partition to the earlier draws.
nodes.title: Tie partition after forgetting the last draw

nodes.summary: The urn law is a probability measure.
nodes.title: Blackwell–MacQueen urn law is a probability measure

nodes.summary: For `n ≤ 2`, `E[∏_{i<n} G(Aᵢ)] = P(X₀ ∈ A₀, …, X_{n-1} ∈ A_{n-1})` for the Blackwell–MacQueen urn. The case `n ≥ 3` is the wanted `lintegral_dirichletProcess_prod`.
nodes.title: Moments of the Dirichlet process for at most two draws

nodes.summary: Exchangeability of the Blackwell–MacQueen urn (Blackwell–MacQueen 1973): relabeling the draws by a permutation does not change their joint law.
nodes.title: Exchangeability of the Blackwell–MacQueen urn

nodes.summary: The predictive law depends measurably on the previous draws.
nodes.title: Measurability of the Pólya urn predictive law

nodes.summary: The event that the draws have a given tie partition is measurable.
nodes.title: Measurability of the tie partition event

nodes.summary: Two indices lie in the same block of `tiePartition xs` iff the entries agree.
nodes.title: Blocks of the tie partition are classes of equal entries

nodes.summary: The predictive law does not depend on the order of the previous draws.
nodes.title: Pólya urn predictive law is invariant under reordering

nodes.summary: `tiePartition xs = π` iff equal entries are exactly the pairs in a common block of `π`.
nodes.title: Characterization of the tie partition

nodes.summary: Where the last draw sits: a new table iff it differs from all earlier draws.
nodes.title: Last draw opens a new block iff it is new

nodes.summary: Where the last draw sits: at the table `B` iff it equals the earlier draws in `B`.
nodes.title: Last draw joins a block iff it matches that block

nodes.summary: The partition of the indices `{0, …, n-1}` into groups of equal entries of `xs`.
nodes.title: Tie partition of a sequence of draws

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
